description: Python's own interpreters, reached from a request. Every channel here was described in the model from the beginning and not one of them had ever matched: the frontend emitted the bare name eval while the rule named builtins.eval, so the language's most direct code-execution primitives were invisible. A name that is neither defined in the file nor imported is the language's own, and saying so connects the two. The negatives are a literal expression and a fixed path.

expected.note: eval compiles and runs whatever it is handed
exec is the same door for statements
the caller names the module the runtime imports
